props.title: DeRolph v. State,
props.objective: Read four rulings from the Ohio Supreme Court and explain why the same answer came back three times.

rows.name: DeRolph I
rows.text: The Ohio Supreme Court rules the school funding system unconstitutional. It leans too heavily on local property taxes, so a child’s school depends on their zip code.

rows.name: DeRolph II
rows.text: The court looks again after the legislature’s changes. Still unconstitutional.

rows.name: DeRolph III
rows.text: A split court says the system could pass if more changes are made. The state asks it to reconsider.

rows.name: DeRolph IV
rows.text: The court vacates its 2001 decision and says it plainly again: unconstitutional. Then it steps back, leaving the fix to the legislature.

rows.name: Still waiting
rows.text: Urban districts like Dayton, Cleveland, Akron and Toledo are still living with the gap, while vouchers can exceed $6,000 for K to 8 and $8,000 for high school.

discuss.question: What does it mean that a child’s school depends on their zip code?
If the court stepped back in 2002, who is responsible for the fix now?

props.sourceText: “Property Taxes, Vouchers & Broken Courts,” DaTruthMeter. Rulings: DeRolph v. State, 1997, 2000, 2001, 2002

props.title: True or false:
props.objective: Commit to an answer before the facts show up. Then trace each fact to its source.

questions.statement: Private philanthropies spend nearly $4 billion a year trying to transform K to 12 education.
questions.note: True. Nearly $4 billion a year, led by the Gates, Broad and Walton foundations.
questions.cite: Cited in “The Corporate Coup of American Education” · Dissent Magazine

questions.statement: For-profit charter schools only exist in a handful of states.
questions.note: False. Over 1,100 charter schools are run for profit across 26 states and D.C., with the highest concentrations in Arizona, Florida, Michigan, Nevada and Ohio.
questions.cite: Cited in “The Corporate Coup of American Education” · Network for Public Education, “Chartered For Profit”

questions.statement: Most of Michigan’s charter schools are run by the public school districts themselves.
questions.note: False. 81 percent of the state’s nearly 300 charter schools contract with private management companies.
questions.cite: Cited in “The Corporate Coup of American Education” · Network for Public Education

props.sourceText: “The Corporate Coup of American Education,” DaTruthMeter

props.heading: What DaTruth*Meter* is

paragraphs.text: DaTruthMeter Media Group was created by Timothy McKinney Jr. to amplify the stories, issues and excellence of the African American community, particularly in education, culture and public impact.
We are an independent Black-owned media company by design, committed to truth-telling, narrative-shifting, and redefining what media can be for Black educators, students and African American culture.

props.belief: We believe in the power of story. We believe in the power of culture. We believe media should do more than inform. *It should ignite change.*
props.intro: Timothy McKinney Jr. is an educator, entrepreneur and public servant.
